questions.prompt: Lesson 6: About how many people in the world are estimated to use smartphones?
questions.explanation: more than four billion people in the world are using smartphones.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: What percentage of Japan's total population used smartphones in 2011?
Lesson 6: By 2018, the rate of smartphone use in Japan had increased to ...
questions.explanation: By 2018, the rate had increased to 64.7%.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: How many minutes a day do Japanese teenagers spend using smartphones just for the Internet?
questions.explanation: Japanese teenagers spend 143 minutes a day ...

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: Who spends 129 minutes a day using smartphones for the Internet?
questions.explanation: people in their 20s spend 129 minutes for the same purpose.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: What do the figures in Section 1 indicate?
choices: We are living in a new culture where the digital world meets the real world
Japan has the most smartphone users
Teenagers do not like the Internet
questions.explanation: These figures indicate that we are now living in a new culture ...

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: Which is NOT given as a way smartphones changed what we do?
choices: The way we relate to people
The way we take care of things in daily life
questions.explanation: relate to people / amuse ourselves / take care of things in our daily lives.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: What lets us stay in constant contact with friends and families?
choices: Texting, emailing, social media, and video chatting
questions.explanation: Texting, emailing, social media, and video chatting let us stay in constant contact ...

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: Which is a practical service of smartphones mentioned in the text?
choices: Doing banking business without going to a bank
questions.explanation: we don't have to go to a bank to do our banking business.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: How can smartphones help in an emergency?
choices: Police officers and firefighters can immediately find where help is needed
questions.explanation: police officers and firefighters can immediately find where their help is needed.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: What can some apps let us monitor?
choices: How much money we have in a bank
How long we slept at school
How far we walked and how many calories we burned
questions.explanation: monitor how far we walked and how many calories we burned.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: Why may using smartphones to entertain very young children be a problem?
choices: Smartphones are too expensive for children
Children watch too many movies at school
Children need contact with other people and the real world to develop fully
questions.explanation: For full mental and physical development, children need contact with other people and the real world.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: According to the text, smartphones may distract us even when ...
choices: they are turned off and in another room
questions.explanation: they may distract us even when they're on silent mode.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: In the study, how many people were asked to solve math problems?
questions.explanation: In one study, 800 people were asked to solve math problems.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: In the study, which group did the best?
choices: Those who left their smartphones in another room
Those who had their smartphones in their pockets
Those who kept their smartphones in front of them
questions.explanation: Group 1 did the best.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: In the study, which group did the worst?
choices: Those who kept their smartphones right in front of them
Those who left their smartphones in another room
Those who had their smartphones in their pockets
questions.explanation: Group 3 did the worst.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: What does the result of the study show?
choices: Smartphones affect how well people can focus their attention
Math problems are easier with smartphones
People in another room are smarter
Smartphones help people solve math problems
questions.explanation: Smartphones had an effect on how well people were able to focus their attention.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: Why could smartphones make us mentally lazy?
choices: They make our lives so easy that we stop trying to remember things
They are too difficult to use
They show us too many books
questions.explanation: We no longer even try to remember meetings and dates.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: For some people, what has the Internet replaced as the main source of information?
questions.explanation: it has replaced books and newspapers as our main source of information.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: Why is believing everything on the Internet dangerous?
questions.explanation: sometimes the Internet spreads lies.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: What ability must we develop, according to the text?
choices: The ability to use many apps
questions.explanation: We must develop the ability to think independently.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: What does the writer suggest at the end?
choices: Maybe we should think about limiting our use of smartphones
We should stop using smartphones completely
questions.explanation: "Moderation in all things" might not be a bad idea.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: What is the main idea of the lesson?
choices: Smartphones bring benefits, but we should use them in a healthy way
Smartphones should be banned in Japan
questions.explanation: 題：Who's in Charge? 便利さと危険の両方を述べ、使い方を考えるよう求めている。

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「It's about time to examine ～」の意味は？
choices: そろそろ〜を調べるべき時だ
〜を調べるのは時間のむだだ
questions.explanation: It's about time to do：そろそろ〜する時だ。

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「bend over ～」の意味は？
questions.explanation: people bending over their smartphones.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「This kind of scene has become so common that we no longer find it strange.」の構文は？
questions.explanation: so common that ...：とてもありふれているので…。

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「no longer」の意味は？
questions.explanation: we no longer find it strange.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「It is estimated that ～」の意味は？

choices: 今も増え続けているから
2018年という過去の時点までの変化を表すから
questions.explanation: By＋過去の時点＋過去完了。

choices: スマートフォンを使う日は1日もない
スマートフォンは1日で壊れる
1日中スマートフォンを使っていない
スマートフォンを使わない日は1日もない

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「they have made us do many things differently」の構文は？
choices: make ＋ O ＋ 原形不定詞（O に〜させる）
questions.explanation: 使役動詞 make。

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「relate to ～」の意味として本文に合うものは？
questions.explanation: the way we relate to people.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「amuse ourselves」の意味は？
questions.explanation: amuse oneself：楽しむ。

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「halfway across the world」の意味は？
choices: 地球の反対側（遠く離れた所）
questions.explanation: even if they are living halfway across the world.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「For instance」の意味は？
questions.explanation: For instance, we don't have to go to a bank ...

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「distract」の意味は？
questions.explanation: Smartphones may distract us.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「pay attention to ～」の意味は？
questions.explanation: to make us pay attention to them.

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「have an effect on ～」の意味は？
questions.explanation: Smartphones had an effect on how well ...

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「rely on ～」の意味は？
questions.explanation: We rely on the Internet for the news ...

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「To make matters worse」の意味は？
choices: 事態をよくするために

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「We don't know what to believe.」の what to believe の意味は？
choices: 信じるべきでないもの
questions.explanation: 疑問詞＋to 不定詞。

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「Believing everything we see on the Internet is not only lazy, it is also dangerous.」の主語 Believing は？
questions.explanation: 動名詞句が主語。

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「Moderation in all things」の意味は？
questions.explanation: moderation：節度・ほどほど。

questions.prompt: Lesson 6:「Until we come to a better understanding ...」の come to ～ の意味は？
questions.explanation: come to a better understanding：よりよく理解するに至る。

questions.prompt: Lesson 6: 次の (   ) に入る語は？ For full mental and physical development, children need contact (   ) other people.
questions.explanation: contact with ～：〜との接触。
